record.original_question: Determine all minor-minimal graphs that do not embed in the spindle pseudosurface.

evidence.quote: Problem 3.6 Find the minor-minimal graphs that do not embed on the spindle.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
The spindle (or pinched sphere) is the pseudosurface obtained from the 2-sphere by identifying two distinct points to a single pinch point. A graph G is said to embed in the spindle if it has a topological embedding in this pseudosurface (edges are interior-disjoint arcs, vertices are mapped to distinct points other than at the pinch point unless one wishes to allow it as a vertex, and any passage through the pinch point is treated as a vertex). The class of graphs embeddable in the spindle is closed under taking minors, so it has a (finite) set of minor-minimal forbidden graphs (excluded minors): graphs G such that G does not embed in the spindle but every proper minor of G does.

Problem. Determine the complete list of all minor-minimal graphs that do not embed in the spindle pseudosurface.
artifact.status_search_result: The complete list is not known. Partial results exist: a computer search has identified 143 excluded minors and 847 topological obstructions for the spindle surface, and the cubic obstruction set has been fully determined (21 cubic graphs). The full minor-minimal obstruction set for general graphs remains open.

status_evidence.title: Some Excluded Minors for the Spindle Surface
status_evidence.snippet: 143 excluded minors and 847 topological obstructions for the spindle surface have been identified via computer search.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial lists of excluded minors are known.

status_evidence.title: Obstructions for embedding cubic graphs on the spindle surface
status_evidence.snippet: Complete list of 21 cubic graphs that form the topological obstruction set for embedding on the spindle surface.
status_evidence.claim: The cubic case is fully resolved, but general case is not.
